sections.h2: The city's share of a New Braunfels tax bill
sections.html:
New Braunfels set a 2025 city rate of $0.408936 per $100 of valuation. Debt service takes $0.193888 of that, and the remaining $0.215048 pays for day-to-day operations and maintenance in the General Fund.

City of New Braunfels 2025 rate split, per $100 of valuation
Rate componentRate per $100
Debt service0.193888
Operations and maintenance0.215048
City total0.408936

That is only one slice. Your school district, Comal County and any special districts bill on their own lines. Staff at Comal Appraisal District can tell you which ones reach your address, and the city's Tax Information page is where a newer rate would appear.

Comal Appraisal District sets values from its Seguin Avenue office and takes calls at 830-625-8597, Monday through Friday. Payments go to the Comal County Tax Assessor-Collector, the office the city names as its collection partner. Values are locked on January 1 and bills go out about October 1. An address that touches Guadalupe County belongs to that county's tax office instead.

  • Value, exemptions and protests: Comal Appraisal District.
  • Payment: the Comal County Tax Assessor-Collector.
  • City hotel tax: the treasury office, 830-221-4369.
  • City main line: 830-221-4000.

The statement can be paid as soon as it lands. Any balance left on February 1 is charged six percent penalty and one percent interest. After that the penalty grows a point a month and halts at twelve percent when July begins, while interest just keeps growing. Where a collection attorney is under contract, up to 20 percent more can be billed.

  • Older and disabled owners can make four payments.
  • Some collectors will draw up a plan lasting as long as 36 months, though only a homestead owner can insist on one.
  • A request to forgive the late charges must be in writing and on file before day 181.

The lien arises each January 1, so whoever held title that morning owes the year's tax, whatever happens to the deed afterward.

Schools must take $140,000 off a homestead's value, and an owner who is older or disabled gets another $60,000 off the school bill. The city and county may choose to add exemptions, so ask the district what New Braunfels and Comal County actually grant. Exemption categories include:

  • Residence homestead, over-65, disabled person, and surviving spouses.
  • Exemptions for a disabled veteran, with a full one for a 100 percent rating on the homestead.
  • Heir property, the 11.35 disaster exemption, and tax deferral for owners 65 or older or disabled.

Form 50-114 is the application, and April 30 is the usual deadline. Bought after January 1 from a seller with no exemption? You can still claim it for the rest of that year. Once granted, it limits yearly growth in appraised value to ten percent.

sections.h2: How to contest a New Braunfels valuation
sections.html:
File with the appraisal review board by May 15. If your notice arrived late, you instead get thirty days from delivery. Homestead notices begin near April 1.

Comal Appraisal District has a taxpayer liaison at 830-626-4874. If the board does not settle it, you can go on to district court or binding arbitration, or to the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the value tops $1,000,000. Keep paying the portion nobody disputes before February 1 so penalties do not build during the appeal.

sections.h2: Short-term rentals and a house sale
sections.html:
A short-term rental here means a one- or two-family dwelling let for under 30 days. The city bars the use in every residential zoning district, requires a special use permit in most non-residential districts, and keeps it out of the floodway. Check this if the house was ever listed on a home-sharing site.

Registering takes a deed, a site plan, a floor plan, at least $500,000 of liability coverage per occurrence and a $206 fee, which includes the first fire inspection. Renewal costs $128 and needs a Fire Marshal visit. No listing may be posted before the permit exists. Since February 1, 2026 hotel tax filings go through an online portal called RentalScape. Operators owe a hotel occupancy tax of 7 percent on top of the state's 6 percent, filed by the 20th of each month even when nothing was earned, and late fees begin at $50. Complaints about unpermitted rentals go to code compliance at 830-221-4074.

If a buyer wants to rent it out, they should phone planning at 830-221-4050 first to find out whether the address can be registered.

A sale can go through with tax unpaid, but the closing changes. Clean title is not possible while delinquent amounts are open, so the title company orders a payoff and takes it from the buyer's funds. The usual order is:

  • Phone the tax assessor-collector's office in Comal County for each unit's balance.
  • Find out if penalty and interest can be waived, which needs a written request before day 181.
  • Give the written payoff to the title company before accepting an offer so you know your net.
  • Settle with the buyer how this year's tax is divided at the closing table.

The owner on January 1 stays liable for that year, so the settlement sheet should spell out who covers which part.

Population has jumped by about a third since the 2020 count of 90,403. The July 2025 estimate is 122,492, and the city had 57,740 in 2010. Roughly 65.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied, with a midpoint value of $339,400. Median household income is $86,021.

sections.h2: What a seller should line up before listing
sections.html:
Before the sign goes up, collect the documents that answer a buyer's first questions. A tidy file shortens the days between offer and closing. Start with the latest statement from every unit that bills the house, then request a current balance from the county's tax office. Include proof of your homestead exemption and jot down the appraisal district's phone number for the buyer, who must file their own.

  • If the house was ever rented for short stays, find the permit, the last fire inspection date and the final hotel tax return.
  • If a protest is pending, note the hearing date so the buyer knows which value the tax will follow.
  • If the owner of record has died, involve the title company at the start. An heir missing from the recorded deeds has to prove an ownership interest to the appraisal district.

A hearing usually turns on what similar nearby houses sold for, so pull those sales before you pick a price. Back tax is paid from your proceeds at closing. A cash buyer skips the lender's timeline but still settles that balance.

faqs.q: What city rate does New Braunfels print for 2025?
faqs.a: $0.408936 per $100 of valuation: $0.193888 for debt service and $0.215048 for operations.

faqs.q: Where does a New Braunfels owner send the tax payment?
faqs.a: Pay the Comal County Tax Assessor-Collector. Questions about value or exemptions go to the Comal Appraisal District at 830-625-8597.

faqs.q: Can I run an Airbnb in a New Braunfels neighborhood?
faqs.a: No. The city bars them in every residential district. Other districts mostly need a special use permit plus a yearly fire inspection.

faqs.q: What is the New Braunfels delinquency date?
faqs.a: February 1. That is when penalty and interest begin, and the penalty stops at twelve percent in July.

faqs.q: Does my buyer have to file a new homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Yes, with Form 50-114 at the Comal Appraisal District. The exemption on file belongs to the seller, and a buyer can claim it for the rest of the year if the seller had none.
